name: Temples of Coastal Karnataka and the Malnad
theme: Great pilgrimage temples of the Karnataka coast and the Western Ghats, from Kateel and Udupi to Gokarna, Sringeri and Horanadu
region: Karnataka (Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Uttara Kannada, Chikkamagaluru)
description: Between the Arabian Sea and the forested crest of the Western Ghats lies a dense chain of renowned temples. On the coast are Kateel, where the goddess Durgaparameshwari is worshipped on an islet in the Nandini river; Udupi, where the Krishna Matha keeps the tradition of Madhvacharya; Kollur, seat of the goddess Mookambika below the Kodachadri hills; Murudeshwar, on a headland above the sea; and Gokarna, home of the Atmalinga. Inland in the Ghats are Kukke Subramanya, the great serpent shrine; Dharmasthala, famed for its charity; Sringeri, the first matha of Adi Shankara on the Tunga; and Horanadu, where Annapoorneshwari feeds every visitor. Coastal roads and Ghat passes join them into a rewarding journey.
